key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion favor dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater porosity reduces long-term corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray process control and service humidity are important considerations for corrosion- and wear-resistant coatings on Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings by detonation spraying under varied parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and long-term corrosion behavior.
Evaluate friction and wear across humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes or humidity ranges, and wear trends involving Si3N4 counterfaces may not transfer to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
